full_judgment:
4. The learned Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Kalkini dismissed the suit on consideration of the evidence on record. The plaintiffs took an appeal there from. The appeal was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Madaripur. The appellate court found that the plaintiffs had been in possession of the suit property for more than 20 years on the basis of a money receipt (Ext.1) and bainapatra (Ext.2) and accordingly came to the conclusion that the plaintiffs were entitled to get a declaration of their title. The appeal was accordingly allowed and the suit was decreed declaring the plaintiffs' title over the suit property and also confirming their possession therein. 

 15. Let as now see if the plaintiffs acquired any title by adverse possession. From a reading of the plaint, it appears that the plaintiffs claimed adverse possession in the body of the plaint. But in the prayer portion they prayed for declaration of title in the 'Kha' schedule property and for confirmation of possession in ejmali along with defendant Nos.2-6 and in the alternative for a decree for specific performance of contract against defendant No.1 in respect of 'Kha' schedule property. But the plaintiffs did not adduce any evidence to prove their case of adverse possession rather they relied upon Exts.1,2 & 3 the receipt, bainapatra and kabala in support of their title. 

 21. In view of the discussions above, we are of the view that the court of appeal and the High Court Division wrongly relied upon the receipt Ext.1, the agreement Ext.2 and the kabala Ext.3 as documents of title in favour of the plaintiffs and accordingly fell in error in decreeing the suit holding that the plaintiffs have title in the suit property. The High Court Division therefore committed an error of law requiring interference by us.
